## Help:Section — how Wikipedia articles are divided into sections and subsections, the auto-generated table of contents, and how to link directly to a specific section via URL anchors (the #Section_name fragment), including how duplicate section names, spaces vs. underscores, and special characters are handled. What is the exact page title and canonical URL?
## Direct answer

- **Exact page title:** `Help:Section` (namespace "Help:", page name "Section")
- **Canonical URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section

(The canonical MediaWiki form uses underscores in place of spaces; this title contains none, so the canonical URL is as shown above. The page is also reachable as `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section?action=raw` etc., but the canonical article URL is the one above.) [1]

## Key content of the page (summary)

**Sections and subsections** [1][5]
- Headings are created with equals signs: `==Level 2==`, `===Level 3==`, … up to `======Level 6======`. The page title itself is the level‑1 heading, so articles start sections at `==`; skipping levels and using `=Level 1=` in articles is discouraged (MOS:HEADINGS).
- Each heading gets an `[edit]` link that opens the editor containing that section's wikitext (including its subsections).

**Auto-generated table of contents (TOC)** [1][3]
- A TOC is generated automatically when a page has more than three headings (i.e., four or more), appearing after the lead, numbered and indented by subsection depth.
- Magic words: `__TOC__` (place the TOC at a chosen spot), `__NOTOC__` (suppress it), `__FORCETOC__` (force it); templates such as `{{TOC limit}}` control displayed depth.

**Linking to a specific section** [1][2][4]
- Wikilinks: `[[Help:Section#Table of contents]]`, or `[[#Section name]]` for the current page; add `|display text` for a label.
- External URL form: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section#Table_of_contents` — the `#fragment` is resolved by the browser, which scrolls to the heading's HTML `id` (MediaWiki auto-generates an id from each heading's text).
- Related templates: `{{Section link}}` / `{{slink}}` (renders "Page § Section"), `{{Anchor}}` and `{{Visible anchor}}` (create extra stable anchors that survive heading renames).

**Spaces vs. underscores** [1][2]
- In fragments, spaces are written as underscores (or `%20` in raw URLs); MediaWiki treats `[[#Table of contents]]` and `[[#Table_of_contents]]` as equivalent.
- The generated HTML `id` replaces spaces with underscores (e.g., `id="Table_of_contents"`).

**Duplicate section names** [1]
- The first occurrence keeps the plain anchor; later duplicates get numeric suffixes in page order: `#History`, `#History_2`, `#History_3`, …
- Renaming or moving a heading breaks incoming anchored links (use `{{Anchor}}` to preserve old anchors).

**Special characters** [1][2][4]
- Most punctuation is kept in anchors; characters that are invalid/ambiguous in a fragment are encoded — e.g., a literal `#` in a heading is dot-encoded (`.23`) in the anchor, and `=` cannot appear in heading markup (use `{{=}}`).
- Non-ASCII characters (é, ü, CJK, etc.) are preserved in the anchor and percent-encoded when used in a URL; such links work when pasted.
- Anchor matching is case-sensitive apart from the first letter, which is auto-capitalized like page titles.

## Wikipedia permanent links (permalinks / oldid): how the 'Permanent link' sidebar tool works, the exact URL format (e.g., en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=...&oldid=...), and why citing the oldid version is recommended when referencing Wikipedia content. ## How the "Permanent link" tool works

Every edit to a Wikipedia page creates a new **revision** with a unique, permanent revision ID number (the "oldid"). Revisions are retained indefinitely (unless deleted/suppressed), so any revision can be viewed forever at its oldid URL [1][2].

- In the desktop skins, the **"Permanent link"** item sits in the **Tools** section (left sidebar in Vector 2010; right-hand "Tools" dropdown in Vector 2022). Clicking it reloads the current page with its current revision ID appended to the URL, pinning that exact snapshot; the page then shows a "Revision as of …" notice [1].
- The resulting link never changes even if the article is edited afterward — it always shows that specific version [1][2].
- A shortcut, **Special:Permalink/PageName**, redirects to the page's current revision (the resolved URL contains the oldid); for citations, the explicit oldid URL is preferred [1].

## URL format

- Canonical: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Example&oldid=123456789` [1][2]
- Short form: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Example?oldid=123456789` [4]
- Title can be omitted, since revision IDs are unique per wiki: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=123456789` [2]
- Diff URLs also use oldid: `…/w/index.php?title=Example&diff=NEW&oldid=OLD` [2][5]

## Why citing the oldid version is recommended

Per **Wikipedia:Citing Wikipedia** [3]:

- Articles change constantly; a plain link shows whatever version exists at click time, which may no longer contain the cited text (or may be vandalized).
- An oldid permalink guarantees readers see **exactly the version the author consulted**, preserving verifiability.
- Recommended practice is to include the permalink URL (with retrieval date) in citations; the "Cite this page" tool (**Special:Cite**) auto-generates citations that already embed the current revision's permanent link [3][7]. The page gives ready-made APA, MLA, Bluebook, and BibTeX examples using oldid URLs [3].

| [1] | Help:Permanent link | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Permanent_link |
| [2] | Help:Page history | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Page_history |

Note: "Wikipedia:Permalink" is a redirect to Help:Permanent link [1].

- **URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_Wikipedia
- **Citation formats it provides:** Ready-made example citations in:

  - **MLA style**
  - **Chicago style**
  - **BibTeX** (a `@misc{...}` entry)

## Retrieving Wikipedia section content programmatically: MediaWiki API action=parse&prop=sections, fetching raw wikitext per section (index.php?title=X&action=raw&section=N), and REST API endpoints for page HTML/sections. What are the exact endpoint URLs and the titles/URLs of the API documentation pages?
## 1. MediaWiki Action API (`action=parse`)

**Endpoint:** `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php` (any wiki: `https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php`)

- **List sections:**
  `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=Earth&prop=sections&format=json&formatversion=2`
  Returns `parse.sections[]` with fields `toclevel`, `level`, `line`, `number`, `index`, `fromtitle`, `byteoffset`, `anchor`, `linkAnchor`. Use the `index` value as the `section=` parameter downstream. Gotcha: transcluded sections get non-numeric indices (`T-1`, `T-2`, …) or empty index (non-editable) — only numeric values work with `&section=` [1][2][3].
- **Wikitext of one section (via API):**
  `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=Earth&prop=wikitext&section=3&format=json&formatversion=2`
  (`section=0` is the lead; use `prop=text` instead of `prop=wikitext` for rendered HTML of that section) [1][2].
- **Docs:**
  - [1] *API:Parse* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parse
  - [2] *API:Parsing wikitext* (tutorial showing exactly this sections→section-wikitext workflow) — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parsing_wikitext
  - [3] Live self-documentation — https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=help&modules=parse

## 2. Raw wikitext via `index.php`

- **Endpoint:**
  `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Earth&action=raw&section=3`
  Omit `&section=` for the whole page; `section=0` = lead. Numbering matches the `index` values from `prop=sections` [4].
- **Docs:**
  - [4] *Manual:Parameters to index.php* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Manual:Parameters_to_index.php
  - Whole-page alternative via Action API (no per-section parameter): `action=query&prop=revisions&titles=X&rvslots=main&rvprop=content` — [5] *API:Revisions* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Revisions

## 3. REST APIs

**a) Wikimedia REST API (RESTBase, `/api/rest_v1/`):**
- Full-page Parsoid HTML: `https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/{title}` (URL-encoded title; optional `/{revision}`). Output wraps each section in `<section data-mw-section-id="N">`, so sections are splittable client-side [6][7].
- Section JSON: `https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/mobile-sections/{title}` (also `mobile-sections-flat`) — **deprecated (announced 2023) and slated for removal; do not build on it** [6][7].
- Interactive docs/spec: root URL `https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/` (spec at `?spec`) [7]; overview: [6] *Wikimedia REST API* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_REST_API

**b) Core MediaWiki REST API (`/w/rest.php/v1/`):**
- `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/rest.php/v1/page/{title}/html` — rendered HTML (Parsoid, with section wrappers)
- `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/rest.php/v1/page/{title}` — page source (wikitext) + metadata; `.../page/{title}/bare` — metadata only [8][9]
- Docs: [8] *REST API* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API ; [9] *REST API/Reference* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API/Reference

**c) Wikimedia API Portal (cross-wiki, authenticated/anon tiers):**
- `https://api.wikimedia.org/core/v1/wikipedia/en/page/{title}` (source), `.../bare`, `.../with_html` (source + rendered HTML)
- Docs: https://api.wikimedia.org/wiki/REST_API and reference https://api.wikimedia.org/wiki/Core_REST_API/Reference [10]

## Practical notes

- Add `origin=*` to Action API calls for browser CORS; set a descriptive `User-Agent` per Wikimedia API policy.
- `formatversion=2` gives cleaner JSON (sections as array of objects).
- The Action API hub page is [11] *API:Main page* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Main_page.

**Sources:** [1] mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parse · [2] mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parsing_wikitext · [3] en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=help&modules=parse · [4] mediawiki.org/wiki/Manual:Parameters_to_index.php · [5] mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Revisions · [6] mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_REST_API · [7] en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/ · [8] mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API · [9] mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API/Reference · [10] api.wikimedia.org/wiki/REST_API · [11] mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Main_page

## Wikipedia:Manual of Style guidance on section headings and article structure (shortcut MOS:HEADINGS) and the Wikipedia:Verifiability policy on whether Wikipedia can be used as a source in research. Exact page titles, shortcuts, and canonical URLs?
## 1. Manual of Style — headings & article structure

**Exact page title:** `Wikipedia:Manual of Style` (the main MoS policy page, shortcut **WP:MOS**)
**Shortcut:** **MOS:HEADINGS** — a redirect to the "Section headings" section of the main Manual of Style page (MOS: is a dedicated pseudo-namespace for MoS shortcuts).
**Canonical URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style#Section_headings (shortcut form: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS:HEADINGS)

**Key guidance at MOS:HEADINGS [1]:**
- Use **sentence case** in headings ("== Rules and principles =="), capitalizing only the first word and proper nouns.
- No terminal punctuation; headings should be concise but descriptive and recognizable.
- Avoid placing links, images, or unusual formatting inside headings; don't skip heading levels (start at `==Level 2==`) — level-skipping is covered in the accessibility guidance (MOS:ACCESS) [1][2].
- Prefer consistent, conventional section names across articles (e.g., "History," "Etymology").

**Article structure:** covered on the subpage `Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Layout` (shortcuts **WP:LAYOUT / MOS:LAYOUT**), URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Layout — prescribes the standard order: lead → table of contents → body sections → appendices ("See also," "Notes," "References," "Bibliography," "Further reading," "External links") → footer elements (navboxes, categories, stub templates) [2].

## 2. Verifiability policy — using Wikipedia as a source

**Exact page title:** `Wikipedia:Verifiability` (one of Wikipedia's three core content policies)
**Shortcuts:** **WP:V** and **WP:VERIFY**
**Canonical URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability

**What it says about Wikipedia-as-source:** the policy section "Wikipedia and sources that mirror or use it" (shortcut **WP:CIRCULAR**, URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia_and_sources_that_mirror_or_use_it) states that Wikipedia articles must **not** be used as sources within Wikipedia — including other-language Wikipedias, mirrors, and forks — because **"Wikipedia is not a reliable source"** and citing it creates circular reporting. Editors must cite the underlying published reliable sources instead [3].

**For external/academic research use**, the related information pages are:
- `Wikipedia:Researching with Wikipedia` — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Researching_with_Wikipedia — Wikipedia is a starting point; verify against its cited sources rather than citing it [4].
- `Wikipedia:Reliability` — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliability — discusses Wikipedia's suitability as a source, noting it is generally not considered citable/authoritative for academic work [5].
- `Wikipedia:Academic use of Wikipedia` and `Wikipedia:Citing Wikipedia` (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_Wikipedia) — guidance for cases where citation is unavoidable [6][7].

**Bottom line:** MOS:HEADINGS lives on the main MoS page (structure detail on MoS/Layout); the Verifiability policy (WP:V) forbids using Wikipedia as a source on Wikipedia itself and, per related pages, treats Wikipedia as a research launchpad — cite the primary/reliable sources it references, not Wikipedia.

### Sources
[1] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style#Section_headings
[2] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Layout
[3] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability
[4] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Researching_with_Wikipedia
[5] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliability
[6] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_Wikipedia
[7] https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Academic_use_of_Wikipedia

*Note: I could not perform a live search in this session; the above reflects the long-standing canonical titles, shortcuts, and URLs of these stable pages as of my last verification — wording details may have drifted slightly.*

## Wikipedia permanent links (permalinks / oldid): how the 'Permanent link' sidebar tool works, the exact URL format (e.g., en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=...&oldid=...), and why citing the oldid version is recommended when referencing Wikipedia content. Which help pages document this, with exact titles and URLs?
## How the "Permanent link" tool works

Every edit to a Wikipedia page creates a new **revision** with a unique, permanent revision ID number (the "oldid"). Revisions are retained indefinitely (unless deleted/suppressed), so any revision can be viewed forever at its oldid URL [1][2].

- In the desktop skins, the **"Permanent link"** item sits in the **Tools** section (left sidebar in Vector 2010; right-hand "Tools" dropdown in Vector 2022). Clicking it reloads the current page with its current revision ID appended to the URL, pinning that exact snapshot; the page then shows a "Revision as of …" notice [1].
- The resulting link never changes even if the article is edited afterward — it always shows that specific version [1][2].
- A shortcut, **Special:Permalink/PageName**, redirects to the page's current revision (the resolved URL contains the oldid); for citations, the explicit oldid URL is preferred [1].

## URL format

- Canonical: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Example&oldid=123456789` [1][2]
- Short form: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Example?oldid=123456789` [4]
- Title can be omitted, since revision IDs are unique per wiki: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=123456789` [2]
- Diff URLs also use oldid: `…/w/index.php?title=Example&diff=NEW&oldid=OLD` [2][5]

## Why citing the oldid version is recommended

Per **Wikipedia:Citing Wikipedia** [3]:

- Articles change constantly; a plain link shows whatever version exists at click time, which may no longer contain the cited text (or may be vandalized).
- An oldid permalink guarantees readers see **exactly the version the author consulted**, preserving verifiability.
- Recommended practice is to include the permalink URL (with retrieval date) in citations; the "Cite this page" tool (**Special:Cite**) auto-generates citations that already embed the current revision's permanent link [3][7]. The page gives ready-made APA, MLA, Bluebook, and BibTeX examples using oldid URLs [3].

## Retrieving Wikipedia section content programmatically: MediaWiki API action=parse&prop=sections, fetching raw wikitext per section (index.php?title=X&action=raw&section=N), and REST API endpoints for page HTML/sections. ## Wikipedia:Manual of Style guidance on section headings and article structure (shortcut MOS:HEADINGS) and the Wikipedia:Verifiability policy on whether Wikipedia can be used as a source in research. Exact page titles, shortcuts, and canonical URLs?
## 1. Manual of Style — headings & article structure

**Exact page title:** `Wikipedia:Manual of Style` (the main MoS policy page, shortcut **WP:MOS**)
**Shortcut:** **MOS:HEADINGS** — a redirect to the "Section headings" section of the main Manual of Style page (MOS: is a dedicated pseudo-namespace for MoS shortcuts).
**Canonical URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style#Section_headings (shortcut form: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS:HEADINGS)

**Key guidance at MOS:HEADINGS [1]:**
- Use **sentence case** in headings ("== Rules and principles =="), capitalizing only the first word and proper nouns.
- No terminal punctuation; headings should be concise but descriptive and recognizable.
- Avoid placing links, images, or unusual formatting inside headings; don't skip heading levels (start at `==Level 2==`) — level-skipping is covered in the accessibility guidance (MOS:ACCESS) [1][2].
- Prefer consistent, conventional section names across articles (e.g., "History," "Etymology").

**Article structure:** covered on the subpage `Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Layout` (shortcuts **WP:LAYOUT / MOS:LAYOUT**), URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Layout — prescribes the standard order: lead → table of contents → body sections → appendices ("See also," "Notes," "References," "Bibliography," "Further reading," "External links") → footer elements (navboxes, categories, stub templates) [2].

## 2. Verifiability policy — using Wikipedia as a source

**Exact page title:** `Wikipedia:Verifiability` (one of Wikipedia's three core content policies)
**Shortcuts:** **WP:V** and **WP:VERIFY**
**Canonical URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability

**What it says about Wikipedia-as-source:** the policy section "Wikipedia and sources that mirror or use it" (shortcut **WP:CIRCULAR**, URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Wikipedia_and_sources_that_mirror_or_use_it) states that Wikipedia articles must **not** be used as sources within Wikipedia — including other-language Wikipedias, mirrors, and forks — because **"Wikipedia is not a reliable source"** and citing it creates circular reporting. Editors must cite the underlying published reliable sources instead [3].

**For external/academic research use**, the related information pages are:
- `Wikipedia:Researching with Wikipedia` — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Researching_with_Wikipedia — Wikipedia is a starting point; verify against its cited sources rather than citing it [4].
- `Wikipedia:Reliability` — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliability — discusses Wikipedia's suitability as a source, noting it is generally not considered citable/authoritative for academic work [5].
- `Wikipedia:Academic use of Wikipedia` and `Wikipedia:Citing Wikipedia` (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_Wikipedia) — guidance for cases where citation is unavoidable [6][7].

**Bottom line:** MOS:HEADINGS lives on the main MoS page (structure detail on MoS/Layout); the Verifiability policy (WP:V) forbids using Wikipedia as a source on Wikipedia itself and, per related pages, treats Wikipedia as a research launchpad — cite the primary/reliable sources it references, not Wikipedia.

## Direct answer

- **Exact page title:** `Help:Section` (namespace "Help:", page name "Section")
- **Canonical URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section

(The canonical MediaWiki form uses underscores in place of spaces; this title contains none, so the canonical URL is as shown above. The page is also reachable as `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section?action=raw` etc., but the canonical article URL is the one above.) [1]

## Key content of the page (summary)

**Sections and subsections** [1][5]
- Headings are created with equals signs: `==Level 2==`, `===Level 3==`, … up to `======Level 6======`. The page title itself is the level‑1 heading, so articles start sections at `==`; skipping levels and using `=Level 1=` in articles is discouraged (MOS:HEADINGS).
- Each heading gets an `[edit]` link that opens the editor containing that section's wikitext (including its subsections).

**Auto-generated table of contents (TOC)** [1][3]
- A TOC is generated automatically when a page has more than three headings (i.e., four or more), appearing after the lead, numbered and indented by subsection depth.
- Magic words: `__TOC__` (place the TOC at a chosen spot), `__NOTOC__` (suppress it), `__FORCETOC__` (force it); templates such as `{{TOC limit}}` control displayed depth.

**Linking to a specific section** [1][2][4]
- Wikilinks: `[[Help:Section#Table of contents]]`, or `[[#Section name]]` for the current page; add `|display text` for a label.
- External URL form: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section#Table_of_contents` — the `#fragment` is resolved by the browser, which scrolls to the heading's HTML `id` (MediaWiki auto-generates an id from each heading's text).
- Related templates: `{{Section link}}` / `{{slink}}` (renders "Page § Section"), `{{Anchor}}` and `{{Visible anchor}}` (create extra stable anchors that survive heading renames).

**Spaces vs. underscores** [1][2]
- In fragments, spaces are written as underscores (or `%20` in raw URLs); MediaWiki treats `[[#Table of contents]]` and `[[#Table_of_contents]]` as equivalent.
- The generated HTML `id` replaces spaces with underscores (e.g., `id="Table_of_contents"`).

**Duplicate section names** [1]
- The first occurrence keeps the plain anchor; later duplicates get numeric suffixes in page order: `#History`, `#History_2`, `#History_3`, …
- Renaming or moving a heading breaks incoming anchored links (use `{{Anchor}}` to preserve old anchors).

**Special characters** [1][2][4]
- Most punctuation is kept in anchors; characters that are invalid/ambiguous in a fragment are encoded — e.g., a literal `#` in a heading is dot-encoded (`.23`) in the anchor, and `=` cannot appear in heading markup (use `{{=}}`).
- Non-ASCII characters (é, ü, CJK, etc.) are preserved in the anchor and percent-encoded when used in a URL; such links work when pasted.
- Anchor matching is case-sensitive apart from the first letter, which is auto-capitalized like page titles.

## Help:Section — how Wikipedia articles are divided into sections and subsections, the auto-generated table of contents, and how to link directly to a specific section via URL anchors (the #Section_name fragment), including how duplicate section names, spaces vs. underscores, and special characters are handled. What is the exact page title and canonical URL?
## Direct answer

- **Exact page title:** `Help:Section` (namespace "Help:", page name "Section")
- **Canonical URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section

(The canonical MediaWiki form uses underscores in place of spaces; this title contains none, so the canonical URL is as shown above. The page is also reachable as `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section?action=raw` etc., but the canonical article URL is the one above.) [1]

## Key content of the page (summary)

**Sections and subsections** [1][5]
- Headings are created with equals signs: `==Level 2==`, `===Level 3==`, … up to `======Level 6======`. The page title itself is the level‑1 heading, so articles start sections at `==`; skipping levels and using `=Level 1=` in articles is discouraged (MOS:HEADINGS).
- Each heading gets an `[edit]` link that opens the editor containing that section's wikitext (including its subsections).

**Auto-generated table of contents (TOC)** [1][3]
- A TOC is generated automatically when a page has more than three headings (i.e., four or more), appearing after the lead, numbered and indented by subsection depth.
- Magic words: `__TOC__` (place the TOC at a chosen spot), `__NOTOC__` (suppress it), `__FORCETOC__` (force it); templates such as `{{TOC limit}}` control displayed depth.

**Linking to a specific section** [1][2][4]
- Wikilinks: `[[Help:Section#Table of contents]]`, or `[[#Section name]]` for the current page; add `|display text` for a label.
- External URL form: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section#Table_of_contents` — the `#fragment` is resolved by the browser, which scrolls to the heading's HTML `id` (MediaWiki auto-generates an id from each heading's text).
- Related templates: `{{Section link}}` / `{{slink}}` (renders "Page § Section"), `{{Anchor}}` and `{{Visible anchor}}` (create extra stable anchors that survive heading renames).

**Spaces vs. underscores** [1][2]
- In fragments, spaces are written as underscores (or `%20` in raw URLs); MediaWiki treats `[[#Table of contents]]` and `[[#Table_of_contents]]` as equivalent.
- The generated HTML `id` replaces spaces with underscores (e.g., `id="Table_of_contents"`).

**Duplicate section names** [1]
- The first occurrence keeps the plain anchor; later duplicates get numeric suffixes in page order: `#History`, `#History_2`, `#History_3`, …
- Renaming or moving a heading breaks incoming anchored links (use `{{Anchor}}` to preserve old anchors).

**Special characters** [1][2][4]
- Most punctuation is kept in anchors; characters that are invalid/ambiguous in a fragment are encoded — e.g., a literal `#` in a heading is dot-encoded (`.23`) in the anchor, and `=` cannot appear in heading markup (use `{{=}}`).
- Non-ASCII characters (é, ü, CJK, etc.) are preserved in the anchor and percent-encoded when used in a URL; such links work when pasted.
- Anchor matching is case-sensitive apart from the first letter, which is auto-capitalized like page titles.

## Sources

[1] "Help:Section" — English Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section
[2] "Help:Link" — English Wikipedia (section linking and anchors) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Link
[3] "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Table of contents" — English Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Table_of_contents

[5] "Wikipedia:Manual of Style" § Section headings — English Wikipedia — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style#Section_headings

## Wikipedia permanent links (permalinks / oldid): how the 'Permanent link' sidebar tool works, the exact URL format (e.g., en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=...&oldid=...), and why citing the oldid version is recommended when referencing Wikipedia content. Which help pages document this, with exact titles and URLs?
## How the "Permanent link" tool works

Every edit to a Wikipedia page creates a new **revision** with a unique, permanent revision ID number (the "oldid"). Revisions are retained indefinitely (unless deleted/suppressed), so any revision can be viewed forever at its oldid URL [1][2].

- In the desktop skins, the **"Permanent link"** item sits in the **Tools** section (left sidebar in Vector 2010; right-hand "Tools" dropdown in Vector 2022). Clicking it reloads the current page with its current revision ID appended to the URL, pinning that exact snapshot; the page then shows a "Revision as of …" notice [1].
- The resulting link never changes even if the article is edited afterward — it always shows that specific version [1][2].
- A shortcut, **Special:Permalink/PageName**, redirects to the page's current revision (the resolved URL contains the oldid); for citations, the explicit oldid URL is preferred [1].

## URL format

- Canonical: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Example&oldid=123456789` [1][2]
- Short form: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Example?oldid=123456789` [4]
- Title can be omitted, since revision IDs are unique per wiki: `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?oldid=123456789` [2]
- Diff URLs also use oldid: `…/w/index.php?title=Example&diff=NEW&oldid=OLD` [2][5]

## Why citing the oldid version is recommended

Per **Wikipedia:Citing Wikipedia** [3]:

- Articles change constantly; a plain link shows whatever version exists at click time, which may no longer contain the cited text (or may be vandalized).
- An oldid permalink guarantees readers see **exactly the version the author consulted**, preserving verifiability.
- Recommended practice is to include the permalink URL (with retrieval date) in citations; the "Cite this page" tool (**Special:Cite**) auto-generates citations that already embed the current revision's permanent link [3][7]. The page gives ready-made APA, MLA, Bluebook, and BibTeX examples using oldid URLs [3].

| [1] | Help:Permanent link | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Permanent_link |

| [6] | Help:Permanent link (MediaWiki.org, multilingual) | https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Help:Permanent_link |
| [7] | Special:Cite ("Cite this page" tool) | https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Cite |

Note: "Wikipedia:Permalink" is a redirect to Help:Permanent link [1].

## Wikipedia:Citing Wikipedia — the exact page title and URL, which citation formats it provides (APA, MLA, Chicago, BibTeX, etc.), and its advice about citing the permanent-link version of an article. Also the page 'Wikipedia:Wikipedia is not a reliable source' — exact title and URL?
**Note:** No live search tools were available in this session, so the following is based on my knowledge of these long‑standing Wikipedia pages. The titles and URLs are stable, but I'd recommend verifying formatting details on the live pages.

## 1. Wikipedia:Citing Wikipedia

- **Exact page title:** `Wikipedia:Citing Wikipedia` (a project/information page in the Wikipedia: namespace)
- **URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_Wikipedia
- **Citation formats it provides:** Ready-made example citations in:
  - **APA style**
  - **MLA style**
  - **Chicago style**
  - **BibTeX** (a `@misc{...}` entry)
  
  It also points users to the **"Cite this page"** tool (in the sidebar's Tools menu), which auto-generates citations in additional formats.
- **Advice on permanent links:** Because Wikipedia articles change constantly, the page advises citing the **exact revision (version) of the article you actually viewed**, not the generic article URL. You get this via the **"Permanent link"** entry in the sidebar Tools menu, which produces a URL of the form:
  `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Article_title&oldid=NNNNNN`
  The example citations (including the BibTeX entry) incorporate this `oldid=` permalink along with the date/time of the revision and your access date, so readers can retrieve precisely the version cited.

## 2. Wikipedia:Wikipedia is not a reliable source

- **Exact page title:** `Wikipedia:Wikipedia is not a reliable source`
- **URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Wikipedia_is_not_a_reliable_source
- **Type:** An essay (commonly referenced via the shortcut **WP:NOTRELIABLE**), explaining that Wikipedia — as a user-generated, tertiary, continuously edited work — should not be cited as a reliable source, including in academic work and within Wikipedia itself (see also WP:CIRCULAR).

**Relationship between the two:** The "Citing Wikipedia" page includes cautionary notes pointing readers toward material like the "not a reliable source" essay and related guidance (e.g., Wikipedia:Academic use), acknowledging that Wikipedia is generally inappropriate as a cited source even while providing citation formats for those who choose to cite it.

## Retrieving Wikipedia section content programmatically: MediaWiki API action=parse&prop=sections, fetching raw wikitext per section (index.php?title=X&action=raw&section=N), and REST API endpoints for page HTML/sections. What are the exact endpoint URLs and the titles/URLs of the API documentation pages?
## 1. MediaWiki Action API (`action=parse`)

**Endpoint:** `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php` (any wiki: `https://{lang}.wikipedia.org/w/api.php`)

- **List sections:**
  `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=Earth&prop=sections&format=json&formatversion=2`
  Returns `parse.sections[]` with fields `toclevel`, `level`, `line`, `number`, `index`, `fromtitle`, `byteoffset`, `anchor`, `linkAnchor`. Use the `index` value as the `section=` parameter downstream. Gotcha: transcluded sections get non-numeric indices (`T-1`, `T-2`, …) or empty index (non-editable) — only numeric values work with `&section=` [1][2][3].
- **Wikitext of one section (via API):**
  `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=parse&page=Earth&prop=wikitext&section=3&format=json&formatversion=2`
  (`section=0` is the lead; use `prop=text` instead of `prop=wikitext` for rendered HTML of that section) [1][2].
- **Docs:**
  - [1] *API:Parse* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parse
  - [2] *API:Parsing wikitext* (tutorial showing exactly this sections→section-wikitext workflow) — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parsing_wikitext
  - [3] Live self-documentation — https://en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=help&modules=parse

## 2. Raw wikitext via `index.php`

- **Endpoint:**
  `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Earth&action=raw&section=3`
  Omit `&section=` for the whole page; `section=0` = lead. Numbering matches the `index` values from `prop=sections` [4].
- **Docs:**
  - [4] *Manual:Parameters to index.php* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Manual:Parameters_to_index.php
  - Whole-page alternative via Action API (no per-section parameter): `action=query&prop=revisions&titles=X&rvslots=main&rvprop=content` — [5] *API:Revisions* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Revisions

## 3. REST APIs

**a) Wikimedia REST API (RESTBase, `/api/rest_v1/`):**
- Full-page Parsoid HTML: `https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/html/{title}` (URL-encoded title; optional `/{revision}`). Output wraps each section in `<section data-mw-section-id="N">`, so sections are splittable client-side [6][7].
- Section JSON: `https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/mobile-sections/{title}` (also `mobile-sections-flat`) — **deprecated (announced 2023) and slated for removal; do not build on it** [6][7].
- Interactive docs/spec: root URL `https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/` (spec at `?spec`) [7]; overview: [6] *Wikimedia REST API* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_REST_API

**b) Core MediaWiki REST API (`/w/rest.php/v1/`):**
- `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/rest.php/v1/page/{title}/html` — rendered HTML (Parsoid, with section wrappers)
- `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/rest.php/v1/page/{title}` — page source (wikitext) + metadata; `.../page/{title}/bare` — metadata only [8][9]
- Docs: [8] *REST API* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API ; [9] *REST API/Reference* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API/Reference

**c) Wikimedia API Portal (cross-wiki, authenticated/anon tiers):**
- `https://api.wikimedia.org/core/v1/wikipedia/en/page/{title}` (source), `.../bare`, `.../with_html` (source + rendered HTML)
- Docs: https://api.wikimedia.org/wiki/REST_API and reference https://api.wikimedia.org/wiki/Core_REST_API/Reference [10]

## Practical notes

- Add `origin=*` to Action API calls for browser CORS; set a descriptive `User-Agent` per Wikimedia API policy.
- `formatversion=2` gives cleaner JSON (sections as array of objects).
- The Action API hub page is [11] *API:Main page* — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Main_page.

**Sources:** [1] mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parse · [2] mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Parsing_wikitext · [3] en.wikipedia.org/w/api.php?action=help&modules=parse · [4] mediawiki.org/wiki/Manual:Parameters_to_index.php · [5] mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Revisions · [6] mediawiki.org/wiki/Wikimedia_REST_API · [7] en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/ · [8] mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API · [9] mediawiki.org/wiki/REST_API/Reference · [10] api.wikimedia.org/wiki/REST_API · [11] mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Main_page

## Wikipedia:Manual of Style guidance on section headings and article structure (shortcut MOS:HEADINGS) and the Wikipedia:Verifiability policy on whether Wikipedia can be used as a source in research. Exact page titles, shortcuts, and canonical URLs?
## 1. Manual of Style — headings & article structure

**Exact page title:** `Wikipedia:Manual of Style` (the main MoS policy page, shortcut **WP:MOS**)
**Shortcut:** **MOS:HEADINGS** — a redirect to the "Section headings" section of the main Manual of Style page (MOS: is a dedicated pseudo-namespace for MoS shortcuts).
**Canonical URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style#Section_headings (shortcut form: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MOS:HEADINGS)

**Key guidance at MOS:HEADINGS [1]:**
- Use **sentence case** in headings ("== Rules and principles =="), capitalizing only the first word and proper nouns.
- No terminal punctuation; headings should be concise but descriptive and recognizable.
- Avoid placing links, images, or unusual formatting inside headings; don't skip heading levels (start at `==Level 2==`) — level-skipping is covered in the accessibility guidance (MOS:ACCESS) [1][2].
- Prefer consistent, conventional section names across articles (e.g., "History," "Etymology").

**Article structure:** covered on the subpage `Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Layout` (shortcuts **WP:LAYOUT / MOS:LAYOUT**), URL: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Layout — prescribes the standard order: lead → table of contents → body sections → appendices ("See also," "Notes," "References," "Bibliography," "Further reading," "External links") → footer elements (navboxes, categories, stub templates) [2].

## 2. Verifiability policy — using Wikipedia as a source

**Exact page title:** `Wikipedia:Verifiability` (one of Wikipedia's three core content policies)
**Shortcuts:** **WP:V** and **WP:VERIFY**
**Canonical URL:** https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability

**Bottom line:** MOS:HEADINGS lives on the main MoS page (structure detail on MoS/Layout); the Verifiability policy (WP:V) forbids using Wikipedia as a source on Wikipedia itself and, per related pages, treats Wikipedia as a research launchpad — cite the primary/reliable sources it references, not Wikipedia.

- A table of contents is auto-generated when a page has four or more headings, and is controlled by the magic words `__TOC__`, `__NOTOC__`, and `__FORCETOC__`.
- Direct links to a section use the URL fragment form `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Section#Table_of_contents`; MediaWiki auto-generates an HTML `id` from each heading, replacing spaces with underscores (or `%20` in raw URLs).
- Duplicate section names receive numeric suffixes in page order (`#History`, `#History_2`, `#History_3`); renaming a heading breaks incoming anchor links (mitigated with `{{Anchor}}` / `{{Visible anchor}}`).
- Special characters are preserved or percent-encoded in anchors (a literal `#` in a heading becomes `.23`); anchor matching is case-sensitive except for the auto-capitalized first letter.

## Sub-Question 2 — Permanent links (oldid permalinks)

**Primary sources:**
- **"Help:Permanent link"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Permanent_link
- **"Help:Page history"** — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:Page_history

**Supporting sources:**

- **"Help:Permanent link"** — MediaWiki.org — https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/Help:Permanent_link
- **"Special:Cite"** (the "Cite this page" tool) — https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special:Cite

**Key findings:**
- Every edit creates a revision with a unique, permanent ID (**oldid**); the "Permanent link" tool in the sidebar Tools menu produces `https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Example&oldid=123456789`, which always shows that exact snapshot.
- Short forms: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Example?oldid=123456789`, or title omitted entirely (`…index.php?oldid=…`) since revision IDs are unique per wiki. `Special:Permalink/PageName` redirects to the current revision.
- Citing the oldid version is recommended because articles change constantly — a plain link may no longer contain the cited text; the permalink guarantees readers see exactly the version consulted, preserving verifiability.
